limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

Governing credit documents not supplied; Missing document; MATERIAL; The executed credit agreement with its amendments through the Sixth Amendment, the collateral agreement and the indentures for the 2036 and 2048 notes are listed as exhibits in the annual report but are not in the source set, and the run settings declare none. Covenant definitions, the guarantor group and collateral cannot be confirmed from a filing summary, and the 2036 notes, described as secured, cannot be ranked against the credit facilities.; Covenant headroom and structural priority are not calculable; Fundamental credit can state covenant terms only as summarised, so any headroom view is conditional on these documents.; Supply the executed credit agreement with amendments through the Sixth Amendment, the collateral agreement, the guarantor list and both indentures.

No covenant ratio or compliance statement at any date; Missing evidence; MATERIAL; No supplied document reports the covenant leverage ratio or states compliance, and the 2026 filings and releases do not mention covenants at all. The annual report gives only the maximum ratio for each quarter after the Antares Vision acquisition, so headroom at 2026-09-30 cannot be measured.; Covenant headroom is conditional; the company's own leverage figure cannot be tested against the covenant definition.; A compliance certificate, a lender presentation or the credit agreement definitions.

Company net leverage cannot be rebuilt; Missing document; MATERIAL; The company's net leverage of 2.5x at 2026-09-30 divides net debt by TTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 460.3 million, which adds Antares Vision earnings from before it was owned. That figure exceeds nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA by USD 142.9 million, made up of Q4 2025 company earnings and Antares Vision pre-acquisition earnings that no supplied document separates. The Q4 2025 release and Antares Vision standalone EBITDA are not supplied, and no FY2025 company Adjusted EBITDA is stated.; Financial foundation and Fundamental credit can quote company leverage as stated but cannot reproduce it or give a like-for-like FY2025 value.; Supply the Q4 2025 earnings release and Antares Vision pre-acquisition Adjusted EBITDA.

Net debt and leverage rest on more than one basis; Conflict; MATERIAL; The annual report states net debt from carrying values net of issuance costs (USD 905.7 million at 2025-12-31), while the 2026 releases use debt before deferred financing costs, USD 30.1 million higher at 2026-09-30. The Q1 and Q2 releases define net leverage on TTM pro forma Adjusted EBITDA, the Q3 release drops the words pro forma without saying the basis changed, and the credit agreement definition is not supplied.; Every leverage figure must carry its basis; no like-for-like series from 2025-12-31 into 2026 can be built from the documents alone.; Company confirmation of the net leverage definition for each quarter.

Segment structure changed in the first quarter of 2026; Conflict; MATERIAL; The annual reports present Crane Payment Innovations and Security and Authentication Technologies. From Q1 2026 the segments are Security and Authentication Technologies and Detection and Traceability Technologies, the latter combining the payment business with Antares Vision. Recast 2025 comparatives are printed for Q1 to Q3 2025 and for backlog, but no recast Q4 2025 or FY2025 segment table is supplied.; Segment trends across FY2025 and 2026 need a bridge; Business & governance and Financial foundation should show segments on one basis at a time.; A recast FY2025 segment table or the Q4 2025 earnings release.

Governance documents not supplied; Missing document; MATERIAL; Directors, independence, committee roles, compensation and ownership are incorporated by reference to the 2026 proxy statement, which is not supplied. Only the executive officer list and an equity compensation plan table are printed, so board quality and ownership concentration cannot be assessed.; Business & governance is limited to management and control disclosures; board and ownership detail is conditional.; Supply the 2026 proxy statement.

Carve-out statements before the Separation; Coverage; MINOR; Statements for periods before 2023-04-03 are combined carve-out statements, so FY2023 includes months of a different perimeter and allocated costs, and trends across the Separation are not like-for-like.; Financial foundation labels FY2023 accordingly; no conclusion changes.; None needed beyond labelling.

Antares Vision accounting is preliminary and pro forma data is thin; Coverage; MINOR; The purchase price allocation is preliminary and open to adjustment. Pro forma net sales and net income are printed for Q1 2026 and Q1 2025 only, with no pro forma EBITDA, cash flow or debt.; Goodwill, intangibles and acquired-business run-rates may change; they are stated as preliminary.; The final allocation in a later filing.

Ratings are dated; Stale evidence; MINOR; Ratings and outlooks are stated as of 2025-12-31 in the annual report. No 2026 filing, release or user input restates them, so any action after the Antares Vision financing is not established.; Fundamental credit labels ratings as of 2025-12-31.; Current agency ratings or reports.

Liquidity detail at 2026-09-30; Missing evidence; MINOR; The revolver commitment (USD 800.0 million) and drawn amount (USD 229.9 million) are stated, but letters of credit or other usage of the revolver, undrawn availability and a principal maturity schedule are not stated for 2026-09-30. Letters of credit appear only at 2025-12-31, under an uncommitted facility. The search covered letter of credit, standby, uncommitted, undrawn, LC, EDC and available capacity.; Liquidity can be stated as cash plus revolver commitment less drawings, with usage unconfirmed.; Company liquidity disclosure at 2026-09-30.

Events after 2026-11-04; Coverage; MINOR; The latest filing was signed 2026-11-04 and the as-of date is 2026-11-18. No later filing is in the set, the Q3 quarterly report has no subsequent-events note, and only a dividend declaration and a conference call date follow in the Q3 release.; Subsequent events up to the cutoff are not established.; Current reports filed after 2026-11-04.

Year-end deleveraging target not quantified; Missing evidence; MINOR; Management says it is on track for a year-end deleveraging target, but no supplied document states its level or basis, so progress cannot be tested.; Fundamental credit treats the target as unquantified.; Earnings call or investor presentation material stating the target.

Debt shown on two bases inside the annual report; Conflict; MINOR; The contractual obligations table shows debt of USD 1,044.2 million at 2025-12-31 against total debt of USD 1,139.5 million in the capital structure table, a difference of USD 95.3 million that the filing does not reconcile. The difference equals revolver borrowings of USD 126.0 million less issuance costs of USD 30.7 million, which is an inference, not a stated reconciliation.; Financial foundation uses balance sheet debt and flags the table basis.; None needed.

Year-end balance sheet line presented differently; Conflict; MINOR; The annual report shows accrued liabilities of USD 273.0 million at 2025-12-31; the 2026 quarterly reports show USD 185.7 million plus a separate contract liabilities line of USD 87.3 million for the same date. The totals tie, so this is a presentation change.; No effect on totals; line items must be compared on one presentation.; None needed.

No market, peer, portfolio or forward inputs; Missing input; MINOR; The run settings hold no quotes, ratings, valuation inputs, peers, portfolio limits, management bridge or forward assumptions. The selected analyses do not need them.; None on the selected analyses; analyses that need them are not selected.; Supply them if market-implied, relative-value or portfolio analyses are wanted.

Antares Vision earnings before 2026-03-31; High; No Antares Vision pre-acquisition EBITDA or pro forma results beyond Q1 net sales and net income; the issuer's TTM Adjusted EBITDA of 460.3 includes it without showing it.; Pro forma leverage and a like-for-like twelve-month EBITDA; last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-30 holds Antares Vision for six months only.; Supply Antares Vision quarterly EBITDA to 2026-03-31 or the issuer's pro forma bridge.

Annual and fourth-quarter 2025 Adjusted EBITDA; High; The issuer states Adjusted EBITDA for quarters and nine months only; no fourth quarter or full year 2025 release is supplied, so Q4 2025 Adjusted EBITDA and FY2025 company net leverage are missing.; Adjusted leverage and cover at every fiscal year end; the quarterly revenue and EBITDA chart has no Q4 2025 EBITDA.; Supply the fourth quarter 2025 earnings release.

Covenant ratio and compliance; High; No supplied document reports the maximum net leverage ratio actual, compliance or headroom for any date; the annual report states only the permitted ratio by quarter.; Covenant headroom at every date.; Supply a compliance certificate or the credit agreement definitions.

Maturities, revolver usage and letters of credit at 2026-09-30; Medium; No principal maturity schedule or letter of credit usage is stated at 2026-09-30; the ladder is at 2025-12-31 and the debt maturities table sums to 95.3 less than carrying value, with the revolver apparently left out.; Liquidity availability and the maturity wall after the 2026 refinancing steps.; Supply the company's liquidity and maturity disclosure at 2026-09-30.

Segment structure changed in 2026; Medium; FY2023 to FY2025 are on CPI and SAT; 2026 and the 2025 nine-month comparatives are on SAT and DTT; FY2025 is not recast.; A single segment series across FY2025 and 2026.; Supply recast FY2025 segment figures.

Net debt and EBITDA definitions differ across documents; Medium; Carrying value against principal, reported against issuer-adjusted EBITDA, and a net leverage definition whose pro forma wording changes between the Q2 and Q3 releases.; Comparability of the house ratios with the company's 2.5x.; Company confirmation of the net leverage definition for each quarter.

Rank, security and guarantors of debt instruments; Medium; The 2036 notes are described as secured senior obligations and the 2048 notes as senior notes, with no statement of their rank against the credit facilities; the guarantor list is not supplied; the revolver and Term Loan A drawn principal and currency split are not stated.; The debt stack lists only the three credit facilities; the notes are left out of it.; Supply the indentures, the credit agreement and the guarantor list.

Lines printed as dashes or not shown; Low; FY2023 equity investment line, FY2023 working capital change, FY2023 acquisition payments and FY2024 term loan proceeds are printed as dashes; interest income is not shown in the quarterly statements; temporary equity is not shown for FY2023 and FY2024; contract liabilities are inside accrued liabilities in the annual reports; investment in equity affiliates has no FY2023 line.; Completeness of those rows; none changes a total or a ratio.; None needed beyond the stated reasons.

Quarter-end balance sheets for March and June 2026; Low; The Q1 and Q2 2026 balance sheets are in the quarterly reports but are not tabulated; net debt data holds year-ends and the latest quarter only.; Quarterly house leverage path after the Antares Vision purchase; the company's own series is in the KPI dashboard.; Tabulate the Q1 and Q2 balance sheets if a quarterly path is wanted.

Antares Vision purchase accounting; Low; The allocation is preliminary; assumed debt is 123.5 in the debt note and 132.3 in the allocation.; Goodwill, intangibles and the net debt effect of the acquisition may change.; Final allocation in a later filing.
Pre-Separation carve-out statements; Low; FY2023 includes months before 2023-04-03 on a carve-out basis.; Trend across FY2023.; None needed beyond labelling.

Subsequent events after 2026-11-04; Low; Nothing dated after the latest quarterly report is supplied, and that report has no subsequent-events note; the Sixth Amendment of 2026-07-02 falls inside Q3.; Events up to the 2026-11-18 cutoff are not established.; Supply current reports filed after 2026-11-04.

facts.label: Governance view
facts.text: Overall, Crane NXT presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is a run of debt-funded acquisitions totalling USD 1,076.4 million since May 2024, which matters because debt rises before the acquired earnings are in the base and goodwill grows, and it implies higher refinancing and impairment risk if integration disappoints. Countervailing evidence is modest dividends, no buybacks and no sponsor or fee leakage. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the pre-acquisition results of Antares Vision. Governance work completed with limitations. facts.label: Key findings

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the company's own deleveraging record. Company net leverage was 2.9x, 2.7x and 2.5x at the three 2026 quarter-ends, company net debt fell USD 150.0 million from 2026-03-31, adjusted free cash flow conversion was 131.8% in Q3 and the order book of USD 715.5 million is 38.57% of last-twelve-months sales. facts.text: Crane NXT is a New York Stock Exchange company formed by the separation of 2023-04-03, when the former Crane Holdings was split into two listed companies and Crane NXT kept the payment and merchandising technologies business, with no sponsor or controlling holder named in the filings read, so extraction risk is not evidenced but cannot be ruled out because board and ownership detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied. Antares Vision personnel hold USD 56.7 million of minority shares in the acquisition vehicle; the Class B shares carry put and call features once converted, but price, timing and settlement form are not disclosed, so a cash call below the parent is possible. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Margins are not stable, and productivity, volume and pricing have offset only part of acquisition amortisation and mix. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: The financial profile is adequate today and weakening in trend. The main supports are cash generation, liquidity and the absence of bank maturities before 2030; the constraints are net debt of 3.03x reported EBITDA, a reported EBITDA margin that fell 6.06 percentage points between FY2023 and the last twelve months, and floating-rate debt at 60.94% of the total. Since FY2023 debt has risen USD 737.6 million while reported EBITDA rose 2.47%, and Antares Vision has still to show its earnings in full. Operating lease payments of USD 102.6 million and purchase obligations of USD 44.8 million at year-end 2025 sit outside reported debt, no factoring, supplier finance or securitisation is disclosed, and the Q2 report showed an interest rate swap inherited with Antares Vision of USD 36.2 million notional that the Q3 report no longer shows. The datapoints that would sharpen the view are the covenant definition and compliance, Antares Vision earnings before 2026-03-31, a maturity schedule, letter of credit usage and swap position at 2026-09-30, and current ratings. Security and authentication carries the profit gain, so a delay cuts currency volumes first; its nine-month operating profit rose USD 40.4 million, and if that gain were lost with net debt unchanged, last-twelve-months reported EBITDA would be USD 333.0 million, net debt over reported EBITDA would rise to 3.40x and EBITDA cover of cash interest would fall to 5.02x. Liquidity would hold, with USD 821.2 million available and no bank maturity before 2030-12-15, and interest would stay covered, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress. The supplied filings and releases support the credit snapshot of Crane NXT through the third quarter of 2026, with limits: covenant headroom, the company's leverage build, governance detail and events after early November cannot be established. Creditors should treat reported leverage and liquidity as company-stated until the missing documents arrive.

## Request

Financial foundation for Crane NXT, Co. (issuer cxt-25445), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway (credit_snapshot). Scope: FY2023 to FY2025 and nine-month 2026 statements, debt at carrying value, leverage and cover on reported EBITDA, with the issuer's adjusted measures beside them.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage on reported earnings rose after the Antares Vision purchase: net debt was 3.03x LTM EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 2.56x at year-end 2025, so creditors carry more debt against earnings that include the acquired business only from March 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 53; calculation C4; calculation C10; calculation C38

EBITDA covered cash interest 5.62x over the last twelve months against 6.35x for FY2025. The company's own net leverage of 2.5x is lower because it adds pre-acquisition earnings of the acquired business and issuer add-backs; the two bases cannot be reconciled from the documents supplied.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C39; calculation C31
### Leverage and coverage

Reported leverage rose at each year-end and again at the latest quarter because debt grew faster than earnings. Net debt over reported EBITDA moved from 1.15x at FY2023 to 1.64x, 2.56x and 3.03x at FY2024, FY2025 and 2026-09-30, while EBITDA stayed between USD 353.3 million and USD 373.4 million. The 2025 De La Rue Authentication purchase and the 2026 Antares Vision purchase were funded mainly with term loans, so debt carries both in full while earnings carry the first from May 2025 and the second from March 2026 only.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C10

Interest cover shows the same shift. Reported EBITDA covered cash interest 8.08x in FY2023 and 8.06x in FY2024, then 6.35x in FY2025 and 5.62x over the last twelve months, because cash interest paid rose from USD 44.1 million in FY2024 to USD 66.4 million as the debt stack grew. Cover remains above 5x, so interest servicing is not the constraint these figures show; whether a covenant ceiling is a constraint cannot be established because no covenant ratio is reported.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C39; calculation C11

The strongest evidence against a rising-leverage reading is the company's own series: 2.9x, 2.7x and 2.5x at the three 2026 quarter-ends, with company net debt falling by USD 150.0 million to USD 1,161.5 million while its TTM Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 448.9 million to USD 460.3 million. That series counts Antares Vision earnings from before it was owned and issuer add-backs; it would prevail if the pre-acquisition amounts were supplied and confirmed on a consistent definition.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-03-31_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX99.1_2026-06-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq2-htm.htm.jsonl, page 9; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C30
### Cash flow and liquidity

Free cash flow was USD 235.5 million over the last twelve months, after operating cash flow of USD 290.3 million and capital expenditure of USD 54.8 million, or 0.63 of reported EBITDA against 0.56 in FY2025. Acquisition payments of USD 225.4 million net of cash acquired and dividends of USD 31.1 million in the nine months of 2026 were paid from that cash flow and from term loan and revolver borrowings, so net debt rose even as free cash flow stayed positive.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C37

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was cash of USD 251.1 million plus an undrawn revolver of USD 570.1 million, USD 821.2 million in total, against USD 231.1 million of borrowings classified as short-term. Letters of credit usage of the revolver is not stated, so availability may be lower. The only maturity ladder is at year-end 2025: USD 9.1 million falls due in 2026 and USD 27.2 million in 2027 to 2028, with USD 326.3 million in 2029 to 2030. It appears to omit the revolver and predates the 2026 refinancing steps, so the maturity wall after 2026 is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C23; calculation C16

Contract liabilities, interest-free customer funding that is not debt, were USD 158.4 million at 2026-09-30, USD 71.1 million above 2025-12-31 on the 2026 presentation, of which USD 46.9 million came with Antares Vision. They fund operations at no interest cost; a fall without matching deliveries would draw on cash, and the filings give no customer deposit terms.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C34
### Data quality and definition risks

Debt appears on three bases in the documents: carrying value on the balance sheet, principal before deferred financing costs in the company's net leverage table (USD 30.1 million higher at 2026-09-30), and the contractual obligations table, which sits USD 95.3 million below carrying value at 2025-12-31 and appears to leave out the revolver. This module uses carrying value and shows the others beside it. Reported EBITDA here is operating profit plus depreciation and amortization; the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA is USD 52.5 million higher for the nine months of 2026 because it adds back transaction, acquisition and restructuring items and starts from net income, so it also holds non-operating income.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation C35; calculation C32; calculation C17

The segment structure changed in the first quarter of 2026, when Antares Vision joined the former CPI business in a new segment. The segment schedule keeps the two structures apart and joins none. Antares Vision earnings before 2026-03-31 are not supplied, so no pro forma EBITDA is stated. The post-balance-sheet table applies year-end FY2025 EBITDA to the added net debt only to show the debt step, and its leverage figure is not a like-for-like pro forma.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Crane NXT is a specialised, acquisition-led technology group whose creditors depend on contract-driven security revenue and a payments business with shrinking organic sales, while the governance evidence supplied is too thin to confirm or rule out a controlling holder.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 115

Debt-funded purchases of USD 1,076.4 million since May 2024 lifted goodwill and intangibles to 60.21% of assets, and one unnamed customer supplied 12.72% of FY2025 sales. Dividends are 19.67% of free cash flow and there are no buybacks, so sponsor and governance risk is rated Medium on incomplete evidence.
Basis: calculation K5; calculation K3; calculation K1; calculation K7
### Key findings

The business is specialised and technology-led, which supports retention but concentrates demand. Crane NXT sells proprietary security features, authentication and payment or inspection equipment to central banks, governments, brands and vending, retail and gaming operators, and describes itself as a principal competitor in most of its markets. One unnamed security customer supplied 12.72% of FY2025 net sales and banknote awards, notably from the U.S. government, vary in timing and size, so a delayed award would cut debt service capacity directly.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 91; calculation K1

Reported growth is acquisition-led while the payments and inspection segment is shrinking organically. In Q3 2026 the detection and traceability segment's organic sales fell 5.3% while acquisitions added 23.1%, and the security segment's organic sales rose 7.2%. Management lowered its full-year sales growth outlook to about 14% from a range of 15% to 17%, which is an untested management statement.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 6

Acquisition appetite is the main behavioural signal and it adds debt faster than earnings. Consideration of USD 1,076.4 million across OpSec, De La Rue Authentication and Antares Vision was funded with revolver and term loan borrowings; balance-sheet debt rose by USD 737.6 million between 2023-12-31 and 2026-09-30 and goodwill and intangibles reached 60.21% of total assets, so an integration miss would appear as impairment as well as lower cash flow.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation K5; calculation K8; calculation K3

Distributions are modest and creditor-neutral on the evidence read. Dividends of USD 39.0 million were 19.67% of FY2025 free cash flow, the quarterly dividend rose by 5.88% to USD 0.18 per share, no open-market repurchases were made in any quarter of 2026, and no sponsor, management fee or related-party leakage appears in the filings read.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-03-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation K7; calculation K9

Ownership and board detail cannot be established, so the risk level rests on behaviour rather than structure. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, but board composition, independence, compensation and beneficial ownership sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied. Management reinvestment in the Antares Vision acquisition vehicle adds minority claims of USD 20.6 million in ordinary shares and USD 36.1 million in Class B shares at fair value, with put and call terms not disclosed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 9

Reporting is adequate for monitoring but silent on covenants. Quarterly reports and releases are timely and audit opinions are unqualified, but revenue recognised over time on U.S. government contracts is a critical audit matter, management excluded De La Rue Authentication from its FY2025 internal-control assessment, and no covenant ratio or compliance statement is published.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 113
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a Medium risk view is the absence of any extraction: no sponsor, no fee stream, no buybacks, dividends at 19.67% of free cash flow, unqualified audits and a backlog of USD 715.5 million of which 94% is due within two years. Management also says it is on track for a year-end deleveraging target and reports falling company net leverage. That view would win if the proxy statement showed dispersed ownership and independent oversight, and if the target proved to be set at a conservative level.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 34; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cxt_exhibit991-pressreleasexq3-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation K7; calculation K23

The view would move to High if the proxy statement showed a controlling holder with a record of debt-funded distributions, if the credit agreement allowed wide restricted payments, or if a further debt-funded acquisition were announced before leverage fell. It would move to Low if the acquired Antares Vision business showed organic growth and the put and call terms were small and fixed.
### Limitations

- The 2026 proxy statement was not supplied, so the Medium rating changes to Low if it shows dispersed beneficial ownership and independent oversight, and to High if it shows a controlling holder with a distribution record.

- The credit agreement and the indentures were not supplied, so capital allocation is judged by what was done and not by what is permitted; broad restricted payment or acquisition capacity would raise the risk level.

- Results of Antares Vision before 2026-03-31 were not supplied, so the enlarged detection and traceability segment shows acquisition-driven growth without a like-for-like trend; a stable acquired base would soften the organic-decline finding.
- The significant customer is unnamed and no contract term is disclosed, so the concentration finding cannot be sized beyond its FY2025 share of sales.
- Put and call terms for management reinvestment are not disclosed, so the cash-call risk below the parent is directional only and could be larger or smaller.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The Antares Vision purchase is the central transaction. Crane NXT bought a 32.3% interest on 2025-12-16 for EUR 117.3 million and completed a tender offer and squeeze-out on 2026-03-31 for EUR 244.2 million, a total consideration of USD 416.9 million including the remeasured earlier interest. It was funded with the new EUR Term Loan B, and Antares Vision personnel reinvested through ordinary and Class B shares of the acquisition vehicle, so part of the acquired equity sits outside the parent. The purchase price allocation is still preliminary, with goodwill of USD 263.1 million and borrowings assumed of USD 132.3 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation K22

The two earlier purchases were also debt-funded. OpSec Security, bought on 2024-05-03 for a USD 270 million base price, drew USD 210.0 million on the revolver. De La Rue Authentication, bought on 2025-05-01 for a GBP 300 million base price (net cash paid USD 391.1 million), was funded with the delayed-draw Term Loan A and brought a consolidated Ghana tax stamp joint venture in which the company owns 49% but controls the board.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-K_2025-12-31_cxt.htm.jsonl, page 83

New debt came only through bank facility amendments. The Fifth Amendment on 2025-12-15 added a EUR 430 million Term Loan B to 2032-12-15, lifted the revolver to USD 800.0 million and extended the revolver and Term Loan A to 2030-12-15. The Sixth Amendment on 2026-07-02 repriced Term Loan B and raised it to EUR 480.0 million at a margin of 2.0% to 2.25%, with the extra proceeds and cash on hand used to repay part of Term Loan A. A 364-day USD 602 million bridge and a USD 831 million backstop were committed in September 2025 and terminated once term debt was placed. No new notes were issued; the 2036 and 2048 notes are the only bonds outstanding.

### Governance view

Overall, Crane NXT presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is a run of debt-funded acquisitions totalling USD 1,076.4 million since May 2024, which matters because debt rises before the acquired earnings are in the base and goodwill grows, and it implies higher refinancing and impairment risk if integration disappoints. Countervailing evidence is modest dividends, no buybacks and no sponsor or fee leakage. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the pre-acquisition results of Antares Vision. Governance work completed with limitations. Crane NXT is a cash-generative specialist whose debt-funded acquisitions have lifted leverage faster than earnings, so creditors depend on integration and banknote award timing to restore deleveraging.

Net debt is 3.03x reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 2.56x at year-end 2025, or 3.57x once the Antares Vision second phase of 2026-03-31 is added to year-end net debt (2.65x with nine months of dividends added instead). Free cash flow of USD 235.5 million over twelve months and liquidity of USD 821.2 million are the main support. The weakest area is payments and inspection, with organic sales down 4.6% over nine months, and covenant headroom cannot be calculated.

### Key findings

Leverage is the central weakness because debt has grown far faster than reported earnings. Balance-sheet debt rose USD 737.6 million between 2023-12-31 and 2026-09-30, while last-twelve-months net sales are 33.32% above FY2023 and reported EBITDA only 2.47% above it, so the EBITDA margin fell from 26.19% to 20.13%. Net debt is 3.03x reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 2.56x at year-end 2025, which is 3.57x once the Antares Vision second phase of 2026-03-31 is added to year-end net debt and 2.65x with the USD 31.1 million of nine-month dividends added alone; debt carries the acquisitions in full while earnings carry Antares Vision only from 2026-03-31.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the company's own deleveraging record. Company net leverage was 2.9x, 2.7x and 2.5x at the three 2026 quarter-ends, company net debt fell USD 150.0 million from 2026-03-31, adjusted free cash flow conversion was 131.8% in Q3 and the order book of USD 715.5 million is 38.57% of last-twelve-months sales. The issuer's adjusted EBITDA margin was 23.0% over nine months against 23.9%, so underlying margin erosion is small. This view would win if Antares Vision earnings before 2026-03-31 and the fourth-quarter 2025 release confirmed the 2.5x on a consistent definition, closing the 0.51x gap to the house ratio, and if a compliance certificate showed wide headroom to the 4.75x maximum due at 2026-12-31 on the same reading of the completion date.

### Limitations

- The credit agreement definitions and compliance certificates were not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable and the leverage-tolerance view rests on the quarterly maximums alone; a definition that adds back more earnings than reported EBITDA would make the position stronger than shown.

- Antares Vision earnings before 2026-03-31 and the fourth-quarter 2025 release were not supplied, so the company's 2.5x cannot be rebuilt; if it were confirmed, the house ratio would overstate leverage by about 0.51x and the cautious view would soften.

- The credit agreement summary does not date the completion of the Antares Vision purchase, so the covenant steps are placed by reading it as 2026-03-31; if the first phase of 2025-12-15 counted instead, each maximum would fall one quarter earlier, to 4.75x at 2026-09-30 and 4.25x from Q1 2027, and the step-down risk would arrive sooner.

- Agency ratings are stated only as of 2025-12-31, before the Antares Vision second phase of 2026-03-31, so the market-access conclusion rests on a dated opinion; a later downgrade would weaken the refinancing view.

- The fourth-quarter estimates are derived from approximate outlook ranges and assume Antares Vision adds the same sales as in Q3, so they show direction only; a firmer outlook could reverse the implied fall in security sales.

- Segment results exist on two structures and FY2025 is not recast, so the margin trend of the payments and inspection business is read from nine-month comparisons only and the fourth-quarter security estimate assumes that segment is unchanged; a recast could change the size of the decline and of the implied fourth-quarter fall.

### Company description

Crane NXT sells proprietary security features, authentication, payment automation and inspection equipment to central banks, governments, brands and vending, retail and gaming operators, and describes itself as a principal competitor in most of its markets. Since 2026 it reports security and authentication with 48.11% of nine-month net sales and detection and traceability with 51.89%, the latter holding the former payments business and Antares Vision from 2026-03-31. The model supports cash-flow visibility through an order book of USD 715.5 million with 94% due within two years, but it concentrates demand in a few government and institutional buyers and exposes results to banknote award timing, so debt service capacity is sound while revenue is lumpy.

### Ownership and group structure

Crane NXT is a New York Stock Exchange company formed by the separation of 2023-04-03, when the former Crane Holdings was split into two listed companies and Crane NXT kept the payment and merchandising technologies business, with no sponsor or controlling holder named in the filings read, so extraction risk is not evidenced but cannot be ruled out because board and ownership detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied. Structural claims matter more than shareholder behaviour here: the credit facilities are secured under a collateral agreement whose guarantor list is not supplied, the 2036 notes are described as secured senior obligations while the 2048 notes are senior notes, and their rank against the facilities is not stated, so the priority of any creditor group is not established. Antares Vision personnel hold USD 56.7 million of minority shares in the acquisition vehicle; the Class B shares carry put and call features once converted, but price, timing and settlement form are not disclosed, so a cash call below the parent is possible.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is only partly predictable: it mixes lumpy government awards, cyclical equipment sales and growing services. Nine-month organic growth of 2.9% came from the currency business, with security and authentication organic sales up 11.6% and detection and traceability down 4.6%, where favourable pricing net of inflation was more than offset by lower hardware and vending volumes. Pricing power therefore exists but does not protect volume, so durability depends on award timing in one segment and equipment demand in the other; the order book gives about two years of visibility, one unnamed customer is 12.72% of sales, and the annual report names global trends in the use of cash and banknote durability as demand risks.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins are not stable, and productivity, volume and pricing have offset only part of acquisition amortisation and mix. Gross margin fell to 40.81% from 42.52% and operating margin to 11.38% from 14.16% over nine months: acquisition amortisation and unfavourable mix cost USD 68.1 million of operating profit, against offsets of USD 34.2 million from productivity and cost actions and USD 31.7 million from higher volumes and pricing net of inflation. The security segment's margin was 12.02% in FY2025 against 23.03% in FY2023, when higher material and manufacturing costs net of pricing cost USD 31.2 million and integration restructuring USD 12.1 million, which shows how input costs and acquired businesses can move profitability. Tariffs are expected to be largely offset by pricing and productivity and are not currently material, but some critical materials come from single or sole-source suppliers and the split of fixed and variable cost is not disclosed, so downside cost flexibility cannot be sized.

### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Reported EBITDA converts into durable free cash flow today, but the conversion is exposed to a capital expenditure step-up and working capital swings. Capital expenditure is 2.95% of last-twelve-months sales, and the 2026 outlook of USD 75 million to USD 80 million implies USD 30.0 million to USD 35.0 million in Q4, about twice the nine-month quarterly average of USD 15.0 million. Customer prepayments recorded as contract liabilities reached USD 158.4 million, up USD 71.1 million of which USD 46.9 million came with Antares Vision, so USD 24.2 million is organic funding that would reverse if deliveries outran new orders, and the company's adjusted free cash flow conversion of -54.5% in Q1 against 131.8% in Q3 shows how uneven cash timing is within a year; the split between maintenance and growth capital expenditure is not disclosed, so flexibility over the maturity wall cannot be tested.

### Competitive forces

Rivalry is real, since the company calls its markets highly competitive and says it is a principal competitor in most of them, but it cites technological differentiation in anti-counterfeiting materials and authentication software, which supports pricing but not volume in a weak cycle. Buyer power is the larger force: central banks and governments buy through awards that vary in timing and size and one customer is 12.72% of sales, so a lost or delayed award reaches debt service capacity directly. Supplier power is moderate, with single or sole-source suppliers for some critical materials that could interrupt production, and substitution is the structural risk to banknote demand, since the annual report names global trends in the use of cash and increased banknote durability. New entrants are not discussed in the filings read, so that force is not established.

### Macro, policy and technology factors

Trade policy, currency and interest rates are the external factors that move credit quality. Tariffs are expected to be largely offset by pricing and productivity and are not currently material to results, but retaliatory measures could cut demand. Half of FY2025 sales were outside the United States and a 10% currency move would change net earnings by USD 7.4 million, which designating the Term Loan B and part of the revolver as net investment hedges partly offsets in equity; and 60.94% of debt floats against 53% at year-end 2025, when the issuer put a 1% rise in rates at USD 6.2 million of interest expense, so the exposure is now larger. Government budgets and central bank procurement drive security demand, while the annual report names advances in payment processing technologies and global trends in the use of cash as risks to demand for payment and banknote products.

### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is adequate today and weakening in trend. The main supports are cash generation, liquidity and the absence of bank maturities before 2030; the constraints are net debt of 3.03x reported EBITDA, a reported EBITDA margin that fell 6.06 percentage points between FY2023 and the last twelve months, and floating-rate debt at 60.94% of the total. Since FY2023 debt has risen USD 737.6 million while reported EBITDA rose 2.47%, and Antares Vision has still to show its earnings in full. Operating lease payments of USD 102.6 million and purchase obligations of USD 44.8 million at year-end 2025 sit outside reported debt, no factoring, supplier finance or securitisation is disclosed, and the Q2 report showed an interest rate swap inherited with Antares Vision of USD 36.2 million notional that the Q3 report no longer shows. The datapoints that would sharpen the view are the covenant definition and compliance, Antares Vision earnings before 2026-03-31, a maturity schedule, letter of credit usage and swap position at 2026-09-30, and current ratings.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the outlook is for slower reported growth and steady cash conversion. Management cut its full-year sales growth outlook to about 14% from 15% to 17%, kept the adjusted EBITDA margin at about 24% and adjusted free cash flow conversion at about 90% to 110%, and narrowed non-operating expense to USD 75 million to USD 80 million. The outlook implies fourth-quarter group sales 7.07% above a year earlier, which becomes a fall of about 3.09% once the USD 50.0 million of Antares Vision sales is added to the base, so organic and currency change is expected to be negative in the quarter. Long-term customer wins that management says enhance visibility, synergy delivery and the order book are tailwinds; lower hardware and vending volumes, trade uncertainty and interest expense that rose 33.11% over nine months are headwinds.

### Downside scenario

The realistic downside starts with a banknote award that slips out of the year while payments and inspection volumes stay weak. Security and authentication carries the profit gain, so a delay cuts currency volumes first; its nine-month operating profit rose USD 40.4 million, and if that gain were lost with net debt unchanged, last-twelve-months reported EBITDA would be USD 333.0 million, net debt over reported EBITDA would rise to 3.40x and EBITDA cover of cash interest would fall to 5.02x. Liquidity would hold, with USD 821.2 million available and no bank maturity before 2030-12-15, and interest would stay covered, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress. The year-end deleveraging target would be missed while the permitted maximum steps down to 4.75x at 2026-12-31, and floating-rate debt at 60.94% would add cost if rates rose; management levers are capital expenditure timing, the dividend of USD 0.18 per share a quarter, cost actions and integration savings, and whether these are enough against a covenant whose definition is not supplied is not established.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Crane NXT presents an adequate business profile supported by specialised security and authentication technology, an order book covering about two years and strong cash generation, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition-led leverage of 3.03x reported EBITDA, a shrinking payments and inspection segment and award concentration. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is 63.07% of reported EBITDA, although it depends on lumpy awards. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on deleveraging towards the company's reported 2.5x on a verified basis, the agencies' view after the Antares Vision financing and covenant headroom through the step-downs. The primary downside path is a delayed banknote award that holds leverage above 3.03x as the covenant maximum falls. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and compliance certificates, Antares Vision earnings before 2026-03-31, the fourth-quarter 2025 release and current ratings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D1; calculation D7; calculation D21; calculation D39; calculation D38
